newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says soldier injured by Ecuadorean mine.
newsitem.headline: Peru says soldier injured by Ecuadorean mine.

text.p: A Peruvian soldier was seriously injured when a mine laid by the Ecuadoran army exploded under his feet in the Andean neighbours' disputed border zone, Peru's Defence Ministry said on Friday.

A ministry statement said Peru would make "the most energetic protest" to an international observer mission monitoring compliance of a peace treaty that ended a short but bloody war on the border in 1995.
The soldier was patrolling inside Peruvian territory when he stepped on the anti-personnel mine. "He suffered the partial mutilation of his right foot and wounds in the body," the statement said.

Peru "deplores once again that events like this keep mutilating and killing soldiers and Peruvian civilians as a result of the Ecuadoran government's irresponsible attitude in sewing mines in our territory since 1995."

The incident came at a tense time in the two nations' traditionally strained relations after Peru this week arrested seven Ecuadoran soldiers inside its border allegedly laying mines and carrying an array of hi-tech weaponry.
Quito said the soldiers lost their way and were "intimidated and psychologically pressured" by their Peruvian counterparts after capture. They were handed back on Thursday to Ecuador's military.

Delegations from both nations were meeting in Brazil this week to seek a permanent solution to a border dispute that stretches back to the beginning of the century and has provoked a string of armed clashes in recent years.
Dozens of soldiers died and hundreds were injured on both sides during the month-long war in 1995.
